description_en: A stone fountain from the medieval period and a Tibetan inscription from approximately 9th-12th century.The monument is located in the heart of Jacha village, on the right bank of the Sinja River. A stone and cement wall encircles the monument, with an access door to the east. The fountain's foundations are lower than the level of circulation. Concrete steps lead to the fountain. In the surrounding wall, a pillar (001) with an eroded inscription was recently inserted. This artefact is most likely found in śikhara temple as part of small vestibule (skt. ardhamaṇḍapa).The fountain has a lower, smaller chamber. Water is supplied by a pipe that runs from the west wall to the east, where the chamber is opened and people collect it. A carved stone lintel (002) with images of three unidentified divinities sits above the pipe's end. Another chamber is located above this one, and it contains a longitudinal slab with an eroded Tibetan inscription from the 9th-12th century (Andolfatto 2019). The upper section of the fountain is pyramidal and śikhara-like, which is a unique regional design for water architecture.The monument's idiosyncrasy and the lack of dated inscriptions complicate dating. It could have been constructed during the mediaeval period.
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number JUM0500_I_001 Sources Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université, p. 55-56. Details Discovered in 2014 CE.

historical_events.event_description: The stele in the second chamber of the fountain contains a 9-line eroded Tibetan inscription. The inscription appears to be an edict, possibly written between the ninth and twelfth centuries. Archaeologist David C. Andolfatto discovered the stele in 2014 CE. It is currently being translated.
